Camp Fire (CA, 2018)
Structure detections vs Carlson · 20 m match

What is this map?

What you are looking at

This map answers the pipeline's first question for the Camp Fire (CA, 2018) (CA_2018_CAMP): did the structure detector find the buildings that Carlson recorded?

Every green point is a Carlson building a predicted structure point landed within 20 m of. Every red point is one nothing landed near. The ring around a point is Carlson's own damage code: a dark ring means the building was destroyed (B), a white ring means it survived (U). Damage is not what this map scores — it is shown so you can see whether the detector fails preferentially on burned-out lots.

Two recall numbers are on the stats chip and they answer different questions. Recall is the product number: of Carlson's buildings, how many did the pipeline find? Recall | in label is the model number: of Carlson's buildings that were actually inside a USA Structures training polygon, how many did the model find? When those two differ a lot, the gap is label coverage, not the network.

Plain-language glossary

  • Carlson — independent building points from Carlson et al. 2025 (USGS data release doi:10.5066/P1QX6UXD). Every point is a building assessed after a U.S. wildfire, 2002–2022. These are evaluation data: they were never used to train the building-detection model.
  • B / U — Carlson's damage codes. B = destroyed / burned; U = surviving / unburned.
  • Chip — a small square aerial photo (512×512 pixels, about 0.6 m per pixel) cut from USDA NAIP imagery. The detection model is trained and run on these tiles.
  • Found / missed — a Carlson point is found when a predicted structure point falls within 20 m of it, and missed otherwise. 20 m is the pipeline's matching radius (validate.match_radius_m).
  • In label — the Carlson point sits inside a USA Structures polygon, i.e. inside a building the model was actually taught to find. Points outside every label are buildings the training labels never showed the model.
  • Precision — of the buildings the model predicted, the share that match a Carlson point. Recall — of Carlson's buildings, the share the model found. F1 — their harmonic mean, one number that punishes being bad at either.
  • Out-of-fold / leave-one-fire-out — every fire is scored by a model trained on the other fires only, so a number for a fire never comes from a model that saw that fire.
  • TP / FP / FN / TN — on the damage maps: predicted destroyed and was (TP), predicted destroyed but survived (FP), predicted surviving but was destroyed (FN), predicted surviving and survived (TN).

Carlson points — found / missed

What you see: one marker per Carlson building inside this fire's chip coverage. Green fill = found within 20 m of a predicted structure point; red fill = missed. Dark ring = destroyed (B); white ring = surviving (U). Hover for the damage code, whether the point was inside a training label, the spatial split, and Carlson's exposure type.

Carlson points that fall outside chip coverage are not on this map and were never scored as misses — the model was not asked to look there.

Source: detections_CA_2018_CAMP.html is built from carlson_scored.gpkg, written by scripts/03_validate_vs_carlson.py.

Predicted structure points

What you see: blue dots — the centre of every building the U-Net predicted on this fire's NAIP chips, after the predicted mask is vectorised and small components are dropped. This is model output, not a surveyed layer; the pipeline's inventory is points, not polygons.

A blue dot with no Carlson point near it is not automatically wrong: Carlson recorded buildings in the fire, so sheds, outbuildings and houses outside the perimeter can be real detections that count as false positives here.

Source: pred_points.gpkg from scripts/03_validate_vs_carlson.py, U-Net checkpoint models/seg_*/best.pt.

USA Structures label polygons

What you see: orange outlines — the building footprints the model was taught to find for this fire: every USA Structures polygon whose IMAGE_DATE precedes ignition. Off by default on a first look; turn it on to see why a red point was missed. A red Carlson point sitting outside every orange polygon was never in the training labels, so it is a label-coverage failure rather than a model failure.

Source: raw/usa_structures/{Fire_ID}_labels_before_*.gpkg, written by scripts/01_build_training_set.py. Post-fire footprint products are never used here — destroyed buildings are missing from them by construction.

Fire-wide recall grid

What you see: the whole fire summarised into 250 m cells, coloured by the share of Carlson points in that cell that were found: red near 0, green near 1, grey where a cell has too few points to read. Hover a cell for its counts.

This layer exists so the detail windows cannot mislead you. Every Carlson point in the fire is in exactly one cell.

How much of the fire you are seeing

This fire has 29,759 points. Drawing them all would make a file no browser opens, so the map shows two things at two scales:

  • Detail windows — 7 squares of 800 m: the 6 with the most points plus the square with the most model failures outside them. Everything inside them is drawn point by point (2,821 points in total). Use the Jump buttons to move between them.
  • Fire-wide grid — every point in the fire summarised into 250 m cells, coloured by the rate in that cell. No point is left out of the grid; the cell size grows automatically if a fire would need more than 6,000 cells.

The windows are the densest squares in the data, not named neighbourhoods, and they are not a random sample: they are the busiest places plus the worst place. Judge the fire-wide numbers from the stats chip and the grid, not from the windows alone.

All of these were computed by scripts/03_validate_vs_carlson.py and read here from summary.json. This map recomputes nothing.

Where the data come from

  • Carlson — Carlson et al. 2025, USGS national structure-loss points 2002–2022 (doi:10.5066/P1QX6UXD). Evaluation only.
  • USA Structures — Oak Ridge National Laboratory / FEMA building outlines (CC BY 4.0), filtered to scenes with IMAGE_DATE before the fire's ignition. The stage-1 training labels.
  • NAIP — USDA National Agriculture Imagery Program, 0.6 m 4-band, via the Microsoft Planetary Computer. What the detection model reads.
  • Sentinel-2 L2A / Landsat Collection 2 L2 — before / after reflectance at each point, via the Planetary Computer. What the damage model reads.
  • CAL FIRE DINS — damage inspection records, the out-of-sample check for fires after Carlson ends.
  • Basemap — Esri World Imagery / Street / Topographic tiles (needs a network connection; nothing else on this page does).

The map draws in geographic coordinates (EPSG:4326). All distances, cell sizes and matching were computed in projected metres (the Carlson USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area frame) before reprojection.
